content.text:
**Finding submitted — IP: deviation at § 14.2.**

- **What's wrong:** § 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for us and leaves us only a *revocable, non-transferable* licence lasting no longer than the Order Form term. That is below even the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense). The perpetual licence in § 13.2 does not rescue it — it reaches only software and Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, not the Deliverable itself.
- **What is already acceptable (not re-drafted):** § 14.1 (Customer Data ownership; Vendor's right confined to processing to provide, secure, support and improve the Services for us), § 14.3 (Vendor retains Vendor Technology; embedded IP carried by § 13.2's perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence), § 14.4 (no joint ownership).
- **Cure:** a single surgical replacement of § 14.2 flipping ownership to Customer with an express assignment, which reaches the preferred position without collateral edits.
